chapter_title: Concerning the Garment of the Waters: how great is
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶4:** How great is the power of the external form that contains divine truth? How far shall [GAP-1] its influence extend into the states of the mind? The divine origin from which all these truths burst forth — how immeasurable must that source be?

**¶6:** [GAP-2] In the state when the Celestial Principle of Good clothed itself with the fundamental goods and truths, and stood firm against the primal enmity that had arisen within falsity from evil, it confronted those great and dominant ruling evils. They are beyond all comprehension, exceeding in magnitude and reach any degree the mind can reckon. At the beginning, when it waged the spiritual combat against them, it brought against them the fire of divine love and the breath of spiritual understanding; and afterward it gave the external containment of divine truths over to the ruling evils that produce spiritual death. So those ruling evils absorbed and consumed those truths, perverting them inwardly. Many [GAP-3] truths poured forth from the external vessel of divine truth [GAP-4] and doctrinal streams proceeded outward. The reception of the ruling evils [GAP-5] those [GAP-6], the aggressive falsities of destruction [GAP-7] labored and brought them forth from within themselves as corrupted forms.

**¶7:** There were seven streams of truth flowing into the reception of each one of them, yet they could not [GAP-8] be brought to satiation within a single interior, to their fullness — because in turn the descent of truth into their interior was consumed by the burning of self-love and its concupiscence. Those ruling evils were like the [GAP-9] of [GAP-10]; they were never emptied of their craving; an influx of truth and [GAP-11] persisted throughout the whole duration of their existence.

**¶8:** The measure of that stream of truth was multiplied sevenfold to fullness, as they flowed [GAP-12] through the external nature of the [GAP-13] truths [GAP-14] in the present state.

**¶9:** [GAP-15] Such is the magnitude of the spiritual combat, since it has [GAP-16] these monstrous persuasions from evil, the towering falsities of self-intelligence. Behold, they are entangled, restrained by divine order, and [GAP-17] held fast in every region of the mind. They are hidden, not made manifest before the perception of any natural-sensory being that dwells upon the plane of spiritual death [GAP-18]. These ruling evils [GAP-19] are made manifest only at last. The entire proprial selfhood will be destroyed and dissolved [GAP-20]; all of it passes away [GAP-21]. It will be destroyed by their raging power, which exceeds in force even the proclamation of divine truth in its ultimates.

**¶10:** This small rivulet of natural knowledge is reckoned as nothing [GAP-22] before the immensity of these divine truths. For the river Tigris upon the natural plane of the mind is but one single stream among thousands upon thousands of streams of truth — drawn from the arcana that remain unrevealed to natural comprehension.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: How great is the power of the garment of the waters? How far shall [it extend]? The source from which all these waters burst forth, how great will it be?

[At] the time when the First Man assumed the elements, and stood [fi]rm against the first enmity that had come about in the Darkness, he defied these great and powerful rulers. They are immeasurable, greater than the extent or size of thousands and ten thousands of parasangs. At the start, when he spread the fight against them, he gave them fire and wind; and afterwards he gave the garment of the waters to the rulers of death. So they, the rulers, drank in and consumed those waters. Many [waters] poured forth from the garment of waters [from which] the rivers flow. The mouth of the rulers [devoured] those [waters], the warriors of destruction [and they] laboured and brought them forth.

There were seven (rivers) flowing in to the mouth of each one of them, as they shall not [suffice] to a single stomach, to their fill; because in turn the descent to its stomach shall burn them with its fire and heat. Those rulers were like the [depths] of [the sea]; they were not emptied; rain and [rivers throughout] their existent days.
The measure of that river was expanded seven times, as they flow [out] of the body of the [living] waters [until] now.

[This] is how great a struggle, since it has [overcome] these creatures of destruction, the mighty giants. Behold, they are entwined, bound, and [sealed] in every place. They are hidden, not revealed before the eyes of every flesh that exists on the land of death [and darkness]. These rulers [shall be] revealed. The entire universe of flesh will be destroyed and dissolved [with them]; all pass away [and perish]. They will be destroyed with their angry voice, which is mightier than the thunder.

this small stream is reckoned [as nothing] before the vastness of these waters. For only one river from thousands of rivers of water, from the secrets that are not revealed, is the river Tigris upon the earth.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading confirms the question asks how far the garment's power will extend its influence, and "it extend" (referring to the garment/power) is grammatically and contextually correct.
"At the time when" is standard Kephalaia temporal phrasing for introducing a cosmogonic episode, confirmed by the spiritual reading's "In the state when."

The spiritual reading translates this as "truths," which in the natural-plane vocabulary of this chapter consistently corresponds to "waters" — the entire passage is about the garment of waters pouring forth.

The spiritual reading states "and doctrinal streams proceeded outward," meaning the rivers flow out from the garment of waters; "from which" provides the necessary relative connector between the source (garment) and the rivers.

The spiritual reading describes "the reception of the ruling evils" consuming/absorbing truths; "devoured" is the natural-plane verb for aggressive consumption through the mouth, complementing the earlier "drank in and consumed" without repeating it.

The entire passage concerns the rulers consuming the waters from the garment; "those waters" continues the subject, with "the warriors of destruction" in apposition describing the rulers who consumed them.

The spiritual reading says the warriors "labored and brought them forth from within themselves as corrupted forms," requiring a conjunction introducing the warriors' subsequent action after consuming the waters; "and they" links the appositive to the main predicate.

The spiritual reading says seven streams of truth "could not be brought to satiation within a single interior"; "suffice" captures the insatiability — seven rivers shall not suffice even for one stomach.

The spiritual reading says the rulers "were never emptied of their craving"; the classic ancient image for insatiable reception is the depths of the sea, which receives all rivers yet is never filled (cf. Ecclesiastes 1:7).
Completing the simile "like the depths of the sea; they were not emptied" — the sea is the universal ancient cosmological image for a receptor that is never filled despite receiving endless waters.

Continuing the sea analogy — the sea receives both rain and rivers yet is never emptied; "rain and rivers throughout their existent days" describes the constant influx the rulers absorbed without being filled.

The spiritual reading says "they flowed through the external nature," corresponding to the rivers flowing out of the body of the waters; "out" connects "flow" to "of the body" in the natural register.

"Living waters" is the signature Manichaean term for the divine waters proceeding from the Living Spirit; the spiritual reading's "truths" corresponds to "living waters" as divine truth in its vivified external form.
The spiritual reading says "in the present state"; "until now" marks temporal continuity — the rivers have flowed from the body of the living waters from the beginning until the present time.
The spiritual reading says "Such is the magnitude of the spiritual combat"; "This" introduces the summarizing declaration in the Kephalaia's expository register: "This is how great a struggle."

The spiritual reading describes prevailing over "monstrous persuasions from evil"; "overcome" is the general verb for the combat's result, followed by the specific modes of restraint (entwined, bound, confined) in the next sentence.

The spiritual reading says "held fast in every region of the mind"; in Manichaean and apocalyptic cosmology, evil powers are "sealed" as the culminating act of binding — forming a triad with "entwined" and "bound."

"Death and darkness" is the standard Manichaean doublet for the realm of evil; the "Land of Darkness" is a foundational Manichaean concept, and pairing it with "death" completes the description of the lower plane.

The spiritual reading says "are made manifest only at last," indicating future revelation; "shall be" creates the necessary contrast with the preceding "hidden, not revealed" — these rulers shall be revealed at the end.

The universe of flesh (proprial selfhood) is destroyed and dissolved together with the rulers it harbors; "with them" ties the destruction of the material world to the fate of the ruling evils, consistent with the Manichaean eschatological dissolution where matter and its dark powers perish together.

"Pass away and perish" is a standard reinforcing doublet in ancient apocalyptic and cosmological literature, expressing total annihilation; the spiritual reading's "all of it passes away" requires a completing intensification before the final destruction sentence.

The spiritual reading explicitly states "is reckoned as nothing before the immensity of these divine truths," and the natural text makes the same comparison — the small stream is negligible before the vast waters.
